To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

thimerosal administered to neonatal rats at doses similar to those in infant vaccines causes numerous neuropathological changes including ischaemic degenerations, "dark" neurons, diminished synaptic protein, and atrophy of glial cells, and that these changes may contribute to neurodevelopmental disorders in children.

the administration of thimerosol, at doses equivalent or higher to those used in human infant vaccines, to rats on the first 15 days of life results in numerous neuropathological changes including ischaemic damage of neurons and astroglial pathology, in the hippocampus of young adult rats.

early postnatal administration to Wistar rats of the vaccine preservative thimerosal, in doses equivalent to those currently used in infant vaccines, or higher, causes numerous neuropathological changes, including neuronal death, vascular damage, diminished synaptic density and atrophy of astrocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of neurotoxicity of thimerosal in developing brain.
the effects of early administration of thimerosol on the developing brain.
the study of neurodevelopmental disorders and their causes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is insufficient to prove that thimerosal causes autism or other developmental disorders.
the results of the study provide evidence for neurotoxic effects in the rat brain after administration of thimerosol at a dose equivalent to that used in infant vaccines.
the thimerosal is not safe and it is a neurotoxic agent, and that it should be replaced with a safe alternative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thimerosal, a preservative, used in vaccines, causes brain damage in developing rats.
thimerosal causes a variety of neuropathological changes at doses used in infant vaccines, and that these changes can be detected in adult animals, suggesting that they are permanent.
thimerosal, an organic mercurial used as a preservative in vaccines, is toxic to developing rat brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neuropathological changes observed in young adult animals treated neonatally with thimerosa were not limited to a single brain region, but involved several brain structures, including prefrontal and parietal cortices, hippocampus and cerebrum.
thimerosal can cause lasting damage to the brain, even when administered in low doses over a short period of time.
the neuropathological changes observed in the brains of young adult rats which had been treated postnatally (neonatal) with thimerosal, are similar to those found in brains of autistic children.
